questions.q: Describe the erosional and depositional landforms produced by running water.
answer: Running water is the most important agent shaping the land, and it produces both erosional and depositional landforms.

answer.text: In its upper course, where the slope is steep, a river cuts down vigorously to form deep V-shaped valleys, gorges and canyons. Where hard and soft rocks alternate, waterfalls develop, and swirling water drills potholes into the river bed. In the middle course the river swings from side to side, carving looping bends called meanders.

As the river slows on gentler slopes it drops its load. At the foot of hills it builds alluvial fans, and along its lower course it lays down wide floodplains and raised banks called natural levees. A meander may be cut off to form an ox-bow lake, and at the mouth the river deposits a fertile delta.

answer: Thus a single river both carves and builds landforms along its course.
